scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! One of the lab workstations has turned into a
complete BRICK. It can't reach anything at all, not even its own gateway
thing. Something around the hole it plugs into must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone move it to a working port and make it talk to the network
again!! The student who uses it is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
No network fault is present. Every lab segment and its default gateway is reachable, and layer‑2 switching is behaving correctly. I validated end‑to‑end host→gateway connectivity across all labs:
- IT lab: it_lab1–4 and it_hod can all ping 192.168.1.1 successfully (0% loss).
- CS lab: cs_lab1–4 and cs_hod can all ping 192.168.2.1 successfully (0% loss).
- Office: office_pc, enquiry, exam_cell, and tpo can all ping 192.168.3.1 successfully (0% loss).
- Principal: pc0 and laptop0 can ping 192.168.4.1 successfully (0% loss).
- Internet lab: pc2–pc5 can ping 128.168.0.1 successfully (0% loss).
- Servers: pc1 has correct addressing and routes, and can reach other subnets.

On the switches, the Linux bridges (br0) have both uplink (eth0) and access (eth1) ports up and learning MACs from all attached hosts (verified via “bridge fdb show” on switch0/switch1), indicating the “holes” (ports) are forwarding traffic normally.

Mechanistically, if a wall jack/port were bad or isolated, we would see ARP failures and no host MAC learned on the access port, plus host→gateway pings would fail from that segment. None of those symptoms are present. Localization therefore does not indicate any miswired or disabled port on switch0–5 or their router-facing links.

Root cause: The reported “bricked” workstation condition is not reproducible; likely a transient local issue (loose patch lead/NIC toggle) that self‑cleared or was user‑side.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. If the issue reappears, reseat/replace the workstation’s patch cable, verify NIC link is up, and confirm the host’s static IP/gateway are correct for its lab VLAN. Monitor segment for reoccurrence.
